gap: No retrieved work causally separates the relevance of added KG context from its quantity under matched supervision budgets. Evidence exists that KG context can help (SG-RAG MOT), hurt when imprecisely selected (IKG/KGSweetSpot), and that scope trades recall against precision (IKG), and DrKGC warns that long graph context adds noise — but these are prompt/inference-time observations or design rationales, not a matched-example, matched-token, equal-length-irrelevant-context comparison of context used as training supervision.

evidence.quote: While KG-based knowledge can enhance LLM reasoning, imprecise selection of relevant knowledge can degrade performance below the zero-shot baseline (where no additional context is provided), highlighting the challenge of integrating KG knowledge without task-specific selection strategies.
While graph paths or subgraphs can be encoded as text prompts, overly long inputs introduce noise and increase computational costs.
We also find out that merging (up to some point) highly overlapping subgraphs and defining an order among the triplets helps the LLM to generate more precise answers.

why_unaddressed: The closest study (IKG/KGSweetSpot) evaluates knowledge representation and relevance filtering in prompts for multiple-choice QA without training a model, so it cannot speak to training supervision. DrKGC optimizes context compactness as a design choice rather than testing it against matched controls. SG-RAG MOT varies context by merging but has no no-context or irrelevant-context arm and no token matching. None isolates relevance from quantity in the training signal.
research_question: Holding the number of training examples and total supervision tokens fixed, does the benefit of adding co-passage context triples to triple/path supervision come from the relevance of those triples (B > C) rather than from the mere presence of additional context, and does explicit relevance selection (D) change the effect?
potential_experiment: A factorial supervision-budget study on a single base model and KG: arms = (A) isolated triple/path, (B) target + passage-derived context triples, (C) target + equal-length irrelevant/random triples, (D) target + relevance-selected context triples (same token count as B), held at matched example counts, matched total supervision tokens, matched prompt template and optimization steps; primary contrast B-vs-C tests relevance, B-vs-D tests selection, A-vs-C tests any extra-context effect. Report one-hop and held-out deeper-hop accuracy plus an error-type decomposition; include a no-fine-tuning LLM baseline. Pre-register the primary metric and the hop split.
verification_required: Verify no recent work already runs a matched-budget context-relevance ablation for KGQA training (targeted search on 2025-2026 KGQA/graph-fine-tuning literature), and confirm that a provenance-bearing dataset with a usable train/dev/test hop split exists.
